label: phase03b_finance_compound_interest
prompt: If I invest $10,000 at 5% annual compound interest for 10 years, how much will I have? Show the formula and step-by-step calculation.
content:
# Compound Interest Calculation

## The Formula

$$A = P\left(1 + \frac{r}{n}\right)^{nt}$$

Where:
| Variable | Meaning | Value |
|----------|---------|-------|
| **A** | Final amount | ? |
| **P** | Principal (initial investment) | $10,000 |
| **r** | Annual interest rate (decimal) | 0.05 |
| **n** | Compounding periods per year | 1 (annual) |
| **t** | Number of years | 10 |

Since compounding is **annual**, the formula simplifies to:

$$A = P(1 + r)^t$$

---

## Step-by-Step Calculation

**Step 1:** Plug in the values
$$A = 10{,}000 \times (1 + 0.05)^{10}$$

**Step 2:** Simplify inside the parentheses
$$A = 10{,}000 \times (1.05)^{10}$$

**Step 3:** Calculate $(1.05)^{10}$

| Year | Calculation | Balance |
|------|------------|---------|
| 1 | 10,000 × 1.05 | $10,500.00 |
| 2 | 10,500 × 1.05 | $11,025.00 |
| 3 | 11,025 × 1.05 | $11,576.25 |
| 4 | 11,576.25 × 1.05 | $12,155.06 |
| 5 | 12,155.06 × 1.05 | $12,762.82 |
| 6 | 12,762.82 × 1.05 | $13,400.96 |
| 7 | 13,400.96 × 1.05 | $14,071.00 |
| 8 | 14,071.00 × 1.05 | $14,774.55 |
| 9 | 14,774.55 × 1.05 | $15,513.28 |
| 10 | 15,513.28 × 1.05 | $16,288.95 |

**Step 4:** Final result
$$A = 10{,}000 \times 1.62889 \approx \$16{,}288.95$$

---

## Summary

> After **10 years**, your **$10,000** investment at **5% annual compound interest** will grow to approximately **$16,288.95**.
>
> - **Total interest earned:** $6,288.95
> - **Note:** The "magic" of compounding is that you earn interest on your interest — in this case, about **$3,288.95** of the total interest is earned from compounding alone.
